title: Epic: Port rate limiting from PR#35 to onboarding PR#32
description:
## Why
PR #35 (feat/otp-endpoints) was closed because we moved to OAuth, but it contained a well-designed reusable rate limiting utility (lib/rate-limit.ts) with HMAC-hashed identifiers, sliding-window counting, fail-open/closed controls, and pre-configured limits. PR #32 (onboarding) has several API endpoints that either lack rate limiting entirely or use ad-hoc inline rate limiting (send-invite-email). We need to port the reusable rate-limit module and integrate it into all onboarding endpoints.

## Success Looks Like
1. lib/rate-limit.ts exists on eco-259-fix-tester-feedback-from-v01 branch with the full utility from PR#35
2. Supabase types include rate_limits table
3. All sensitive API endpoints use the shared rate limiter
4. send-invite-email refactored from inline rate limiting to use the shared utility
5. .env.example updated with RATE_LIMIT_HMAC_KEY
6. Build passes (bun run build)

## Scope
- Target branch: eco-259-fix-tester-feedback-from-v01
- Source: origin/feat/otp-endpoints (lib/rate-limit.ts)
- Do NOT port OTP-specific code (email_otps, otp routes, resend email, layer editor changes)
- Only port the generic rate limiting infrastructure and wire it into existing onboarding endpoints

title: Epic: Address CodeRabbit review feedback on PR#34 interactive analytics dashboard
description:
## Context
PR#34 (feat/interactive-analytics-mode) introduces an interactive analytics dashboard at /internal/analytics/interactive. CodeRabbit reviewed the PR and found 9 actionable issues and 9 nitpick improvements across data precision, accessibility, event handling, and code quality.

## Goals
- Fix all 9 actionable CodeRabbit review comments (bugs, a11y, correctness)
- Address the 9 nitpick suggestions (code quality, maintainability)
- All work targets the feat/interactive-analytics-mode branch

## Scope
Files in:
- app/internal/analytics/interactive/ (page, components, hooks)
- app/internal/analytics/page.tsx
- components/global/modals/upload/layer/editor.tsx

## Success
- All CodeRabbit actionable items resolved
- Build passes (bun run build)
- No new lint errors

title: Fix animated completion rate decimal precision
description: ## Files - app/internal/analytics/interactive/components/cards/CardCompletionRate.tsx (modify) ## What to do The useAnimatedNumber hook (line 36 of useAnimatedNumber.ts) uses Math.round() on each frame, so when CardCompletionRate passes a value like 33.3, the animation rounds to integers and .toFixed(1) always shows '.0'. Fix: animate a scaled integer (multiply by 10), then divide by 10 for display. Change line 11-14: ```ts const animatedRate = useAnimatedNumber( Math.round(data.completionRate * 10), // was: Math.round(data.completionRate * 10) / 10 { delay: 500, duration: 1200, enabled: isActive } ); ``` Change line 36: ```tsx {(animatedRate / 10).toFixed(1)}% ``` Leave animatedCompletions and animatedStarts unchanged. ## Don't - Modify useAnimatedNumber.ts itself - Change any other card components - Change animation timing or delays
acceptance_criteria:
1. When completionRate is 33.3, the animated number smoothly counts up and displays '33.3%' (not '33.0%')
2. When completionRate is 0, displays '0.0%'
3. When completionRate is 100, displays '100.0%'
4. animatedCompletions and animatedStarts still display as integers
5. Build passes: bun run build
close_reason: 992e5cc fix: animate scaled integer for decimal precision in completion rate

title: Derive currentCardId from cards array and guard background decorations
description:
## Files
- app/internal/analytics/interactive/page.tsx (modify)
- app/internal/analytics/interactive/components/InteractiveModeBackground.tsx (modify)

## What to do
Two maintainability improvements:

### 1. Remove CARD_IDS duplication in page.tsx (lines 78-87)
The CARD_IDS array duplicates the order of the cards array. If one changes, themes silently desync.

Delete the CARD_IDS constant (lines 78-87).
Change line 138 from:
```ts
const currentCardId = CARD_IDS[currentCard] || 'welcome';
```
to:
```ts
const currentCardId = cards[currentCard]?.id ?? 'welcome';
```

### 2. Guard against missing decorations in InteractiveModeBackground.tsx (line 32)
If a theme has fewer decorations than STAR_POSITIONS entries, accessing theme.decorations[i] returns undefined, causing a runtime error when accessing .char and .color.

Change line 32 from:
```ts
const decoration = theme.decorations[i];
```
to:
```ts
const decoration = theme.decorations[i] ?? { char: '✦', color: 'var(--bumi-white-80)' };
```

## Don't
- Change the cards array definition
- Modify CARD_THEMES or CARD_TO_TRACK in interactiveTheme.ts
- Change STAR_POSITIONS
- Alter the visual appearance of decorations when data is present
acceptance_criteria:
1. CARD_IDS constant is removed from page.tsx
2. currentCardId is derived from cards[currentCard]?.id
3. Theme mapping still works correctly for all 8 cards
4. If a theme has fewer than 6 decorations, a default decoration renders instead of crashing
5. Build passes: bun run build

title: Extract animation duration constant and add missing isPlaying state update in hooks
description:
## Files
- app/internal/analytics/interactive/hooks/useCardNavigation.ts (modify)
- app/internal/analytics/interactive/hooks/useBackgroundMusic.ts (modify)

## What to do
Two small improvements:

### 1. Extract animation duration constant in useCardNavigation.ts
The 500ms timeout is repeated on lines 49, 64, 80, 97, 115. Extract it:

Add before the export:
```ts
const ANIMATION_DURATION_MS = 500;
```

Replace all 5 occurrences of the literal 500 in setTimeout calls with ANIMATION_DURATION_MS.

### 2. Track isPlaying state on track switch in useBackgroundMusic.ts
In the track-switch effect (lines 44-63), when switching tracks, isPlaying state is not updated. If the play() call on line 59 fails silently (the .catch), the UI may show incorrect playback state.

After line 59, add state tracking:
```ts
if (!isMuted && newAudio) {
    newAudio.currentTime = 0;
    newAudio.play()
        .then(() => setIsPlaying(true))
        .catch(() => setIsPlaying(false));
} else {
    setIsPlaying(false);
}
```

Note: The current code has .catch(() => { }) which swallows the error silently. The fix adds state tracking to both success and failure paths.

## Don't
- Change the animation duration value (keep it 500ms)
- Change the navigation logic
- Modify the startMusic or toggleMute callbacks
- Add new hooks or state variables beyond what's described
acceptance_criteria:
1. ANIMATION_DURATION_MS constant exists and is used in all 5 setTimeout calls in useCardNavigation.ts
2. No literal 500 remains in setTimeout calls in useCardNavigation.ts
3. isPlaying state updates correctly when track switch succeeds or fails
4. Build passes: bun run build

title: Clamp bar widths in CardFunnelAnalysis and CardTimeDistribution
description:
## Files
- app/internal/analytics/interactive/components/cards/CardFunnelAnalysis.tsx (modify)
- app/internal/analytics/interactive/components/cards/CardTimeDistribution.tsx (modify)

## What to do
Bar widths computed from percentages can exceed 100%% or go negative if backend data is inconsistent. Clamp all computed widths to [0, 100].

### CardFunnelAnalysis.tsx
Line 52 — change:
```ts
const barWidth = data.totalFlowStarts > 0 ? (step.users / data.totalFlowStarts) * 100 : 0;
```
to:
```ts
const rawWidth = data.totalFlowStarts > 0 ? (step.users / data.totalFlowStarts) * 100 : 0;
const barWidth = Math.min(100, Math.max(0, rawWidth));
```

Also check lines 98-103 for any other width calculations in this file and apply the same clamping pattern.

### CardTimeDistribution.tsx
Line 55 — change:
```tsx
animate={isActive ? { width: `${Math.max(item.percentage, 5)}%%` } : { width: 0 }}
```
to:
```tsx
animate={isActive ? { width: `${Math.min(100, Math.max(item.percentage, 5))}%%` } : { width: 0 }}
```

## Don't
- Change animation timing or transitions
- Modify the visual appearance (colors, heights, etc.)
- Add new imports
acceptance_criteria:
1. In CardFunnelAnalysis, barWidth is always in [0, 100] regardless of step.users or totalFlowStarts values
2. In CardTimeDistribution, bar width is always in [5, 100] (5%% minimum preserved, 100%% maximum enforced)
3. No visual regression for normal data (values already in range)
4. Build passes: bun run build
close_reason: 8352f4f fix: clamp bar widths to [0,100] in CardFunnelAnalysis and CardTimeDistribution

title: Fix aria-labels and nested interactive elements in InteractiveModeHeader
description:
## Files
- app/internal/analytics/interactive/components/InteractiveModeHeader.tsx (modify)

## What to do
Two issues in this file:

### 1. Incorrect aria-label on music button (line 87)
Current: aria-label={isMuted ? 'Unmute music' : 'Mute music'}
This doesn't account for the !isPlaying state. Fix:

```tsx
aria-label={!isPlaying ? 'Start music' : isMuted ? 'Unmute music' : 'Mute music'}
```

### 2. Nested interactive elements: Link wrapping button (lines 68-75)
A <button> is nested inside a <Link> (which renders as <a>). This is invalid HTML.

Replace:
```tsx
<Link href="/internal/analytics">
    <button className={styles.exitButton} aria-label="Close">
        ✕
    </button>
</Link>
```
with:
```tsx
<Link href="/internal/analytics" className={styles.exitButton} aria-label="Close">
    ✕
</Link>
```

## Don't
- Change the music toggle logic (handleMusicClick)
- Modify the progress bar section
- Change any styling classes
- Add new imports
acceptance_criteria:
1. When music has not started (!isPlaying), aria-label reads 'Start music'
2. When music is playing and muted, aria-label reads 'Unmute music'
3. When music is playing and not muted, aria-label reads 'Mute music'
4. The exit button is a single <Link> element (no nested <button>)
5. The exit button still navigates to /internal/analytics
6. The exit button still has aria-label='Close'
7. Build passes: bun run build

title: Fix error rendering in layer editor to show readable messages
description:
## Files - components/global/modals/upload/layer/editor.tsx (modify) ## What to do Line 222 renders errors with String(error), which produces '[object Object]' for tRPC errors. Change lines 220-224 from: ```tsx {error && (
{String(error)}
)} ``` to: ```tsx {error && (
{(error as { message?: string })?.message ?? String(error)}
)} ``` This uses optional chaining to prefer error.message (works for Error objects and tRPC errors) and falls back to String(error) for unknown shapes. ## Don't - Change the error variable type or where it's defined - Add try/catch blocks - Modify the isFeatureDisabled banner - Import new error handling utilities
acceptance_criteria:

2. When error is a tRPC error with .message property, displays the message string
3. When error is a plain string, displays the string
4. When error is null, nothing renders (existing behavior preserved)
5. Build passes: bun run build
